approach: Record the branch checked out at dispatch in a new optional `dispatch_branch` on the `athena.job/1` record (written where run/mod.rs builds the `Job` at dispatch). `land::plan` takes a `&Dispatched` (`Unknown`, `Branch(name)`, `Detached`) and reads `git.current_branch()` itself. If the dispatch branch is known and differs from the current one, `plan` returns a new `Plan::OtherBranch(reason)` before the ancestor check. The reason names the dispatch branch. Records without the field are `Unknown` and keep today's behavior. Retry (close.rs ~484) treats `OtherBranch` like `Stale`: it bails and the job stays blocked, writing nothing. First landing (close.rs ~228) records a `stale` outcome as today only when the checked-out branch already holds the job's `job.json`. If it does not, `land_or_block` bails with a message naming the dispatch branch and writes nothing. Reason: the closing score is recomputed by the gate from the job's records in the committed tree (athena-gate/src/jobs.rs:301-319, `expected_score`; athena-score/src/lib.rs:412-452 reads the job record, readings and invocations). On a branch that lacks them it would differ from the score close.rs builds from the in-memory job, so the gate would refuse Athena's own commit. Edits to run/mod.rs (the `Job` literal names every field) and lifecycle.rs (the `go` flow can only be driven there) are outside the listed deliverables. Both are justified here and named in the final report.

decisions.choice: Store `dispatch_branch: Option<String>` on `records::Job` with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, set in run/mod.rs at dispatch (the `Job` literal ~888, using `self.git.current_branch()?`). `Some("")` means a detached HEAD at dispatch. The convention is stated in three places: the field's doc comment, the land.rs header, and the reason text for that case ('dispatched on a detached HEAD (recorded as an empty branch name)').
decisions.reason: No existing dispatch-time field holds the branch. `Outcome.branch` (close.rs:56, records.rs ~872) is the branch at finish. `Job.base_commit` is a commit id. `Job` is committed before work starts, and both landing paths already hold it (`ctx.job.job`, `job.job`). `default` plus `skip_serializing_if` follow the existing `pin` field, so old records parse under `deny_unknown_fields` and keep the old behavior as `Unknown`. Finding 5 allowed keeping the empty-string sentinel if named explicitly; that is done.

rejected.why: It is written at finish, so it is the value to compare against, not the dispatch branch.
Two fields allow an invalid pair (a branch name plus detached=true). The one field plus a documented convention is smaller, and the reading asks for a single recorded branch.
A detached dispatch could not be told from a job dispatched before this change, which must keep the old behavior.

rejected.option: Add the field to the candidate record
rejected.why: Candidate has /1 and /2 schemas with parse rules in `AnyRecord::parse`, and is written after the producer runs, not at dispatch.

rejected.option: Derive the branch at verification start
rejected.why: The branch can change between dispatch and verification, and a blocked retry runs in a later session. Only a record written at dispatch survives both.

decisions.choice: The rule is the first step of `land::plan`, which gains a `&Dispatched` parameter and reads `git.current_branch()` itself. A new variant `Plan::OtherBranch(String)` carries the reason. The only matches on `Plan` are close.rs:229/257, close.rs:485/488, and the land.rs tests (grep of crates/).
decisions.reason: close.rs:228 and :484 are the only callers of `plan`, so one rule covers first landing and retry. Reading the branch inside `plan`, from the repository that supplies `head`, stops a caller from passing a branch that disagrees with `head`. A separate variant lets the first-landing caller choose between recording stale and bailing, without matching on reason text.

rejected.option: Check in each caller in close.rs
rejected.why: The rule would be written twice and could drift; it is not the root-cause location.

rejected.option: Caller passes the current branch as a string
rejected.why: A caller or test could pass a branch that is not the one `head` came from.
First landing must tell a branch mismatch from other stale reasons, because the stale records commit is safe only when the branch holds the job's records (decision 3).

decisions.choice: Detached HEAD: a detached dispatch is always refused. A branch dispatch that finishes on a detached HEAD is also refused. The reason text says which case it is.
decisions.reason: The accepted assumption treats a differing or absent branch as refused. A detached HEAD names no branch, so the rule cannot confirm the job is landing where it was dispatched.

rejected.option: Land when both dispatch and finish are detached and the base is an ancestor
rejected.why: That is today's behavior for the one case the rule cannot verify.

decisions.choice: First landing, branch mismatch (answers findings 3 and 4). `land_or_block` looks at the job in `Records::load(&self.git, &head)` (`records.jobs.get(id).and_then(|j| j.job.as_ref())`). (a) If the checked-out branch holds the job's `job.json`, `Plan::OtherBranch` is handled like `Plan::Stale`: the existing stale outcome is committed on the checked-out branch with a gate-checked records-only commit. (b) If it does not hold it, `land_or_block` bails before `build_commit`: 'job X was dispatched on `A`, but `B` is checked out and has no records of the job; nothing was recorded or landed. Check out `A`, or `athena retry X`'. Nothing is written, and the checked-out tip is unchanged. In both cases the dispatch branch A never gets an outcome. The job there has `job.json` and no outcome, so `status` shows it as `interrupted` (`state_name`, status.rs:1616-1619; listed in `open`, status.rs:1671-1675). `athena go X` then bails 'was interrupted' and points to `athena retry` and `athena close` (run/mod.rs:346-359). The test asserts this.
decisions.reason: `score_on` builds the closing score from the in-memory job and all its readings and invocations (close.rs:23-37). The gate recomputes it from the commit's tree (jobs.rs:301-319, `expected_score`). On a branch with no `job.json`, readings or earlier invocations, `accepted`, `reading_accepted` and the invocation list differ (athena-score/src/lib.rs:412-452), so `build_commit` would bail with 'the gate refused Athena's own commit'. The branch holds `job.json` exactly when it contains the dispatch commit, and the dispatch commit comes after the ask and reading commits, so `job.json` present implies the job's earlier records are present. In case (a) the gate sees the same shape as any stale outcome today. This is read from the code, not run; the case (b) test is the check.

rejected.option: Always commit the stale outcome on the checked-out branch
rejected.why: On a branch forked before dispatch the gate would likely refuse the commit, and `go` would fail with a gate error instead of a clear reason.

rejected.option: Always bail and record nothing on first landing
rejected.why: The accepted reading and criterion 1 say stale. Case (a) is safe, so recording it keeps the stated outcome there.

rejected.option: Copy the job's records onto the checked-out branch so the stale commit passes the gate
rejected.why: It would write a job's whole record set to a branch it never ran on, and the invocation records are in earlier commits, not in the closing files. That is a larger change than the landing decision.

rejected.option: Write the stale outcome onto the dispatch branch without checking it out
rejected.why: `Git` has no update-ref method (athena-git/src/lib.rs). It would move a ref that another worktree may have checked out, and it is auto-switching territory, out of scope.

decisions.choice: Retry path (`retry_landing`): `Plan::Stale(reason) | Plan::OtherBranch(reason)` share the existing bail (close.rs:485-487). The job stays blocked and nothing is committed.
decisions.reason: The blocked outcome is already on the dispatch branch, and it can still land after the user checks that branch out again. The retry only runs where the blocked records are visible, so the records problem of decision 4 does not arise.

rejected.option: Write a new outcome on the retry
rejected.why: The job is already blocked, and the existing bail for other stale reasons leaves it so.

decisions.choice: No refusal-corpus case. `refusal_corpus` is not a demonstration.
decisions.reason: The rule compares a stored branch name with the current one. It parses no request text, reading or stem list, so there is no input form to map to a case in crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs.

rejected.why: The corpus covers reading and request text, and no such input reaches this rule.

decisions.reason: Its `athena.job/1` row is not an exhaustive field list (the existing `pin` and `class_of_work` are not in it), and no test compares it with the struct. The field is documented on the struct.

rejected.option: Add the field to the docs row
rejected.why: It widens scope to a file outside the deliverables for a row that is already partial.

risks.risk: The stale records commit on a branch lacking the job's records is likely refused by the gate. This is read from the code (jobs.rs:301-319, athena-score/src/lib.rs:412-452), not run.
risks.mitigation: `land_or_block` checks for the job's `job.json` on `head` first and bails before `build_commit` if it is missing. Criterion 1 test (b) exercises exactly that branch shape and asserts nothing is written.

risks.risk: Case (a) holds `job.json` but a later record the gate needs is missing from the branch (a fork part-way through the job).
risks.mitigation: All of a job's records before the dispatch commit were committed before it, so `job.json` present implies the rest. If the gate still refuses, `build_commit` fails before `advance`, so nothing is written and the error names the gate. Test (a) runs `check_history()`.

risks.risk: Test (b)'s hook switches to `other` while verification is running, and later steps in `go` read records or files from the new HEAD, so the test fails for an unrelated reason.
risks.mitigation: The producer reads the code after the hook point first (step 1). If something reads the dispatch records from HEAD, it uses the nearest hook point that works. The assertion on the error text names the dispatch branch, so a different failure is visible.

risks.risk: An existing integration test dispatches on one branch and finishes on another, and now refuses.
risks.mitigation: Run the full `cargo test --locked` in step 8. Change a test only where it truly switches branches between dispatch and finish, with a comment saying so, and report which. Do not weaken the rule.

Use `?` so a git failure stops the dispatch loudly instead of recording no branch. The same call already runs at finish (close.rs:56).

risks.mitigation: This is the intended meaning of 'dispatched from'. Every dispatch goes through the one literal at run/mod.rs:888.

demonstrations.method: Two integration tests drive the real `Athena::go` flow in crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs, plus a land.rs unit test on `plan`. Test (a), `a_job_finished_on_a_branch_with_its_records_goes_stale`: the fixture is on `main`. A guarded-once `Scenario.during_verification` hook runs `git checkout -q -b other` (so `other` holds the dispatch commit) and stores `other`'s tip in an `Arc<Mutex<String>>`. After `go` it asserts: state `Stale` and the reason contains `main`; `other`'s new tip has the captured tip as its parent; `git diff --name-only` between them lists only paths under `records/`; README.md has no greeting; `fingerprint(new tip, base)` equals `fingerprint(base, base)`; `main`'s tip is unchanged; `job.json` at the dispatch commit has `dispatch_branch` `main`; `check_history()` reports no violations. After `git checkout -q main` it asserts `status()` lists the job in `open` with state `interrupted`, and `go` on it returns an error containing `interrupted`. Test (b), `a_job_finished_on_a_branch_without_its_records_changes_nothing`: before `ask`, the test runs `git branch other` at the fixture's initial tip, so `other` has the base but not the dispatch commit. The hook captures `main`'s tip and runs `git checkout -q other`. It asserts `go` returns an error naming `main` and saying nothing was recorded or landed; `other`'s tip equals the initial tip exactly; README.md has no greeting; `git ls-tree -r --name-only other` lists nothing under `records/jobs/`; after `git checkout -q main`, `status()` shows the job `interrupted`. The unit test `a_job_dispatched_elsewhere_is_refused_on_another_branch` calls `plan` with `Dispatched::Branch("main")` on a repository whose current branch is `other`, with the base an ancestor of head, and expects `Plan::OtherBranch` naming `main`.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test lifecycle a_job_finished_on_a_branch && cargo test --locked -p athena-core land::tests::a_job_dispatched_elsewhere
demonstrations.observes: A job finished on another branch lands nothing: state `stale` with a reason naming the dispatch branch when the other branch holds the job's records; no commit and an error naming the dispatch branch when it does not. The other branch gets no job content in either case, and in case (b) its tip is unchanged. The gate accepts the case (a) records commit. After returning, the dispatch branch shows the job as `interrupted`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check, `plan` returns `Plan::Tree` because the base is an ancestor of `other`'s head, and the job lands on `other` with state `Landed`. The state, reason, README, fingerprint, tip and records assertions in (a) and (b) all fail. The unit test fails because `plan` returns `Plan::Tree`.

demonstrations.method: New tests in the records.rs test module. (a) A `Job` with `dispatch_branch: Some("main")` and one with `Some("")` pass through `AnyRecord::Job(..).to_json()`, `AnyRecord::parse` and `check_record_file`, and equal the original. (b) A job JSON with no `dispatch_branch` key parses, yields `None`, and serializes without the key. (c) The existing `Job` test literal (~4850) gets `dispatch_branch: None` and still round-trips.
demonstrations.observes: All records round-trip tests pass, with and without the new field.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the field were missing from `Job`, `deny_unknown_fields` would make `check_record_file` and `AnyRecord::parse` reject the record that has it. If it lacked `#[serde(default)]`, the record without it would fail to parse.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `AnyRecord::parse` and `check_record_file` (records.rs ~3045). The tests build records in memory and need no fixture. They exist today. The store.rs `dispatched()` literal (~597) is updated in step 3.

demonstrations.method: The refusals are shown by the criterion 1 and 3 tests. The '5% of newly refused readings' figure is an expectation about use, not measured by any test, and the plan does not claim to check it. The full suite shows the extra refusals are limited to jobs that switch branches between dispatch and finish.
demonstrations.observes: The full suite passes. New refusals appear only in the new tests; same-branch landings in lifecycle, drain, reconcile, trailer_stop and history_pr_head are unchanged (each creates its branch before `ask`, or does not dispatch a job across branches).
demonstrations.fails_without: A rule that refused ordinary same-branch landings would fail the existing landing tests, such as `landed` in lifecycle.rs near line 223.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `Athena::go` through the existing integration suite. The fixtures exist today.

open_questions: User: Criterion 1 says B's tip is unchanged and the outcome is stale. The code cannot give both everywhere. When B holds the job's records (it was forked after dispatch), the plan records a stale outcome on B, so B's tip moves by one records-only commit and gains no job content. When B lacks them (it was forked before dispatch), the plan records nothing, B's tip is unchanged, and `go` ends with an error naming the dispatch branch; the job shows as interrupted on the dispatch branch. This is because the gate would likely refuse a stale score commit on a branch without the job's records. Please confirm this reading of the wording.
User: Criterion 8's '5% of newly refused readings' is read as an expectation about use, not a threshold a test enforces. No code or data in the repository measures a refusal rate. Please confirm.
